# Roy Gardner

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Roy  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c26 P15](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0015)</sub>

## Appearance

Roy is described as adorably handsome with gloriously deep, black, velvety dark eyes. His sister Dorothy notes that she would look like him if she had dark eyes instead of hazel ones.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c25 P48](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0048), [v3 c26 P19](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0019), [v3 c36 P24](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0024)_

## Personality

Roy is polite, clever, soft-spoken, and possesses unfailing, deferential courtesy that charms older figures like Aunt Jamesina. He courts poetically and romanticizes his gestures, such as sending long-stemmed roses or white orchids. Though sincere and deeply devoted in his affection, his mannerisms can feel overly flawless, perfectly worded, or slightly rigid when faced with unexpected disappointment.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P42](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0042), [v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047), [v3 c26 P1](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0001), [v3 c26 P5](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0005), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c38 P17](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0017), [v3 c38 P25](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0025), [v3 c38 P27](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0027)_

## Traits

- Adorably handsome  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- Clever  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- Deferential and polite  <sub>[v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018)</sub>
- Romantic and poetic  <sub>[v3 c25 P42](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0042), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c38 P17](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0017)</sub>

## Abilities

- Eloquent speech and poetic wooing  <sub>[v3 c25 P42](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0042), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c38 P17](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0017)</sub>

## Goals

- To court and marry Anne Shirley  <sub>[v3 c26 P4](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0004), [v3 c38 P17](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0017)</sub>

## History

Roy first meets Anne Shirley in a park during a heavy rainstorm, rescuing her when her umbrella turns inside out. Shortly after, he sends a dozen long-stemmed roses with a poetic rhyme to her residence at Patty's Place and receives permission to call on her. Over the next two years at Redmond College, Roy intensely courts Anne, frequently bringing her orchids, walking her home, and attending campus functions with her. His family later visits Patty's Place, where his sister Dorothy confides how fondly Roy speaks of Anne. Eventually, Roy takes Anne to the harbour pavilion where they first met and proposes marriage in a impeccably crafted speech. However, Anne realizes she does not truly love him and refuses his proposal, leaving Roy heartbroken and bitter as he bids her a final farewell.

_Sources: [v3 c25 P42](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0042), [v3 c25 P44](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0044), [v3 c26 P1](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0001), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c26 P19](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0019), [v3 c36 P22](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0022), [v3 c36 P32](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0032), [v3 c38 P17](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0017), [v3 c38 P18](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0018), [v3 c38 P25](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0025), [v3 c38 P27](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0027), [v3 c38 P32](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0032)_

## Background by volume

- Belongs to the wealthy, high-society Gardner family in Kingsport  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- His father is deceased  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- Had to leave college two years prior to travel abroad with his ill mother  <sub>[v3 c25 P47](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0047)</sub>
- Shares a close confidence with his younger sister Dorothy  <sub>[v3 c36 P32](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0032)</sub>

## Quotes

> So you’ve just been amusing yourself these two years?  <sub>[v3 c38 P25](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0025)</sub>

> You have ruined my life.  <sub>[v3 c38 P27](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0027)</sub>

> Then—good-bye. I can’t understand it—I can’t believe you are not the woman I’ve believed you to be. But reproaches are idle between us. You are the only woman I can ever love. I thank you for your friendship, at least. Good-bye, Anne.  <sub>[v3 c38 P32](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0032)</sub>
